description: Sage-specific brand contract: approved phrases, illustration concepts, negative constraints, framing directions, and default adoption scene/style anchor. Loaded at import by brand_gen/sage_generation_contract.py and mutated through typed bgen verbs (update-sage-approved-phrases, add-sage-framing-direction, remove-sage-framing-direction, update-sage-negative-constraints, set-sage-default-adoption, set-sage-default-style-anchor, update-sage-illustration-concepts, update-sage-brand-anchor-sources).
approved_phrases: curated skills improve agent performance by +16.2pp
someone has to govern the standard library
agents find and use better workflows with less repeated setup
illustration_concepts: curated capability selected from library, then used
library shelf / capability slots / finished artifact
routed lattice / path motif derived from the mark
negative_constraints: do not default to semi-realistic 3D/isometric robot or humanoid agent scenes unless explicitly requested
do not default to robots or people editing/pushing artifacts into a central hub unless explicitly requested
do not default to a central switchboard/control-room composition unless explicitly requested
no raw prompt dump / random capability card deck / glowing light-bulb idea icon
default_adoption_scene: a library manifest opens a default capability slot in an abstract thin harness; a finished work artifact appears downstream without showing robots or humanoid agents
default_style_anchor: flat editorial system illustration: standard-library shelf, routed lattice/path motifs, warm palette, print restraint, no semi-realistic robot workshop

framing_directions.label: chosen-not-collected editorial sieve
framing_directions.keywords: chosen not collected selection curation judgment good bad worse mismatch focused sets
framing_directions.source_cues: Chosen, not collected; gap is selection; bad skills make agents worse; focused sets outperform comprehensive dumps
framing_directions.adoption_scene: an editorial selection sieve rejects noisy/generated skills and lets one curated capability become a runtime default
framing_directions.style_anchor: flat editorial sieve/gate composition with rejected noise outside the frame, one chosen capability artifact, restrained proof typography
framing_directions.directive: Frame Sage as selection rather than storage: a visible editorial sieve chooses one good capability and filters out harmful skill noise.

framing_directions.label: fat-skills / thin-harness missing layer
framing_directions.keywords: fat skills thin harness missing layer hermes tan architecture whose skills should agent use
framing_directions.source_cues: Tan named thin harness/fat skills; Hermes named per-agent loop; Sage names the missing layer above both
framing_directions.adoption_scene: a thin runtime harness sits below a maintained layer of fat skills; one governed skill drops into the harness as the default
framing_directions.style_anchor: layered architectural section drawing: thin base harness, thick curated skill layer above, one active default slot, no character workshop
framing_directions.directive: Frame Sage as the missing layer above thin harnesses: maintained fat skills become trusted defaults for runtimes.

framing_directions.label: tokenized taste canon
framing_directions.keywords: tokenized taste canon editorial function attributed funded tipped economic value value capture
framing_directions.source_cues: Sage scales tokenized taste; people who know what's good can be attributed, funded, tipped, and governed into the canon
framing_directions.adoption_scene: curator taste signals become attributed economic value: one judgment is funded, promoted into canon, and visibly rewarded
framing_directions.style_anchor: premium editorial/economic-value composition with taste signals, attribution marks, value flow, and one promoted capability; not an installation pipeline
framing_directions.directive: Frame Sage as tokenized taste becoming economic value: human editorial judgment gets attributed, rewarded, and turned into shared canon.

framing_directions.label: curator compensation flywheel
framing_directions.keywords: curator compensation compensated labor tips bounties paid libraries creator value capture rewards economic incentives
framing_directions.source_cues: Curation is compensated labor; creators capture value through tips, bounties, paid libraries, governed canon, and reflections
framing_directions.adoption_scene: a curator's judgment moves through attribution, tip/bounty reward, paid-library inclusion, and visible value capture
framing_directions.style_anchor: editorial economic flywheel / value ledger composition: curator signal, reward markers, paid library, canon seal; no runtime process diagram
framing_directions.directive: Frame Sage as the economics of curation: good judgment becomes compensated labor and repeatable value capture.

framing_directions.label: market knowledge ledger
framing_directions.keywords: market knowledge repeated use visible authorship purchases bounty wins forks trusted curators evidence graph
framing_directions.source_cues: Skill effectiveness is emergent market knowledge: repeated use, visible authorship, tips, purchases, bounty wins, forks, governed inclusion, trusted curators
framing_directions.adoption_scene: signals of use, authorship, purchases, tips, forks, and governed inclusion accumulate into a market-knowledge ledger around a capability
framing_directions.style_anchor: premium editorial ledger/evidence-map composition with sparse value signals and provenance marks; no fake dashboard, no process pipeline
framing_directions.directive: Frame Sage as market knowledge: value emerges from repeated use, visible authorship, purchases, forks, tips, and trusted curation.

framing_directions.label: ownership as steering rights
framing_directions.source_cues: Ownership as steering rights — economic framing, not committee framing
framing_directions.adoption_scene: ownership tokens act as steering rights over which capabilities become defaults, with value flowing to the curators who steer well
framing_directions.style_anchor: editorial ownership/steering-rights composition: directional rights, value allocation, canon boundary; no proposal/vote theatre
framing_directions.directive: Frame Sage as ownership/steering rights: economic control over default capabilities, not a governance-process scene.

framing_directions.label: execution DAG compounds
framing_directions.keywords: dag dependency molecule compound orchestrator graph retrieval semantic seeding execution metadata atoms compounds
framing_directions.source_cues: Graph retrieval combines semantic seeding, dependency resolution, execution DAG metadata, and molecule/compound orchestrators
framing_directions.adoption_scene: small capability atoms resolve into a compound execution DAG, and the compound becomes the reusable default workflow
framing_directions.style_anchor: clear DAG/compound diagram with few nodes, dependency paths, one highlighted reusable workflow, no generic network cloud
framing_directions.directive: Frame Sage as execution compounds: atoms stay legible, but governed DAGs make the reusable workflow dependable.

framing_directions.label: RLM memory loop
framing_directions.keywords: rlm reinforcement learning memory prompt response captures suggestion weights local retrieval usage evidence
framing_directions.source_cues: RLM captures prompt-response pairs and improves future skill suggestions; confidence is local retrieval evidence, not protocol ranking
framing_directions.adoption_scene: local usage traces form a memory loop that suggests a better capability default next time without pretending to be a global ranking
framing_directions.style_anchor: quiet memory-loop diagram: captured traces, local suggestion weights, chosen capability, bounded evidence labels
framing_directions.directive: Frame Sage as memory improving future defaults: local traces inform suggestions while governance/provenance remains separate.

framing_directions.label: standard-library canon
framing_directions.keywords: standard library canon shelf shelves library maintained shared infrastructure
framing_directions.source_cues: Someone has to govern the standard library; communities govern skill libraries once work becomes shared infrastructure
framing_directions.adoption_scene: a maintained canon/standard-library object supplies one governed capability as the runtime default
framing_directions.style_anchor: flat editorial canon/library composition with maintained shelves, one promoted artifact, warm palette, print restraint
framing_directions.directive: Frame Sage as the governed standard library: maintained canon, not random marketplace inventory.

framing_directions.label: category-creator constellation map
framing_directions.keywords: category creator constellation white-space landscape adjacent projects agent-native skill improvement network
framing_directions.source_cues: Sage is a category creator above adjacent projects: agent-native skill improvement network with value capture
framing_directions.adoption_scene: a constellation of adjacent tools sits below a newly named Sage category layer that routes capability defaults
framing_directions.style_anchor: editorial category map/constellation with whitespace, named category boundary, no competitor dashboard or feature race
framing_directions.directive: Frame Sage as category creation: a new named layer organizes adjacent tools rather than competing as another feature box.

framing_directions.label: transit route map
framing_directions.keywords: transit route map subway metro path lattice
framing_directions.adoption_scene: capability routes branch from a governed library map into runtime default paths and finished outputs
framing_directions.style_anchor: flat transit-map/system-diagram illustration with routed lattice paths, strong negative space, restrained labels
framing_directions.directive: Frame Sage as a route map: governed library as the station/source, capability paths as selectable defaults, finished outcomes at endpoints.

framing_directions.label: capability specimen sheet
framing_directions.keywords: specimen sheet catalog index cards tiles archive proof sheet
framing_directions.adoption_scene: a curated capability specimen is selected from a governed catalog and appears as an abstract runtime default
framing_directions.style_anchor: editorial specimen-sheet composition: catalog tiles, one selected capability, deterministic type, no fake UI chrome
framing_directions.directive: Frame Sage as a catalog/specimen sheet: many governed capabilities exist, one is selected and becomes the default.

framing_directions.label: proof poster
framing_directions.keywords: proof poster benchmark evidence metric claim
framing_directions.adoption_scene: a proof claim and library manifest demonstrate how a capability becomes a default and improves the finished workflow
framing_directions.style_anchor: message-first proof poster with one artifact, one metric/proof payload, one small provenance mark
framing_directions.directive: Frame Sage as a proof poster: one library artifact plus one concrete evidence payload, not a dashboard.

framing_directions.label: runtime slot blueprint
framing_directions.adoption_scene: an abstract runtime blueprint exposes empty default slots; a governed capability fills one slot and produces a finished artifact
framing_directions.style_anchor: blueprint/system schematic with large abstract slots, thin connector paths, no humanoid character hero
framing_directions.directive: Frame Sage as a runtime-slot blueprint: abstract slots make the default-setting mechanism visible without staging agents as characters.

framing_directions.label: explicit switchboard only
framing_directions.keywords: switchboard exchange control-room control room routing board hub
framing_directions.source_cues: conversation fallback only; too general for default Sage framing
framing_directions.adoption_scene: an exchange/routing board selects a governed capability as a runtime default; the finished work appears downstream
framing_directions.style_anchor: graphic exchange-board composition with distributed routes, not a character workshop or centered logo
framing_directions.directive: Use switchboard/routing-board framing only when explicitly requested; it is too general to be the default Sage idea.

framing_directions.label: abstract agent workbench
framing_directions.adoption_scene: a deliberately abstract workbench shows capability artifacts becoming defaults for a runtime, with any agent presence subordinate
framing_directions.style_anchor: flat/productive workbench abstraction; if characters appear, keep them symbolic and secondary, not semi-realistic robots
framing_directions.directive: Use an agent/workbench framing only if specifically requested; keep any characters abstract and subordinate to the capability artifact.
